Yeah because everybody can just come in here and make an input and that's a good thing. We can't force people not to investigate further into an obviously fake site. They said beware false paths and put a PGP key for a reason. One of the reasons and prime examples is (pi).mobi. You saw the runes that are a part of that "riddle"? They are just basic switching , no encryption whatsoever. Not to mention the runes are slightly different too. Then it leads to a message that all is hidden in the vibrati ( or sth like that , I checked that as soon as it came out) and other nonsense. If you want to proceed into that and waste time , suit yourself lol.
Going by this logic everything that has a cicada stamp on it can be the "true path" . They always used PGP and then what? They stopped just to delude people into focusing on stuff with no PGP and suddenly they dumped liber primus which was the core of 2k14 riddle? I'm not buying that. The "Verify OpenPGP" that comes after the "Beware false paths" message is there for a reason.... Just so you won't waste time on something that's not verified.. They also monitor the internet , this page and (pi) . They are fully aware of people trying to mimic them hence the additional info about "false paths" . What you believe in is your business ;)
Update : Yeah it went like this : "The key in the message is in the vibrati . Seek with your ears not your eyes" . Makes total sense when you compare it to the liber primus message lol. It just doesn't add up...
